Both letters characterize industry attacks as propaganda that distorts facts and maligns or obstructs government action, and both contrast legitimate consideration on the merits with coercive or misleading tactics serving private interests. C12 and C04 share related concerns about attacks on official integrity and ethics in government, but their language and argumentative structure are less closely aligned with the child.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"The organized campaign of misrepresentation now being waged against the staff report on oil cartels prepared in your Commission is a good illustration of attempted coercion and intimidation.","parent_excerpt":"I have been shocked in recent days at the extraordinary propaganda campaign that has been unleashed against this bill by the real estate lobby. I do not recall ever having witnessed a more deliberate campaign of misrepresentation and distortion","explanation":"The distinctive formulation of an industry-backed 'campaign of misrepresentation' against a government measure or report is materially shared."},{"child_excerpt":"I think there can be no excuse, for example, for the vituperative attacks upon the motives and even the loyalty of those responsible for the report.","parent_excerpt":"The propaganda of the real estate lobby consistently misstates the explicit provisions of the bill, consistently misrepresents what will be the actual effect of the bill, and consistently distorts the facts","explanation":"Both passages condemn propaganda directed against government work as systematic distortion rather than engagement with its merits."},{"child_excerpt":"all too often the unethical approach is used by some business interests","parent_excerpt":"Yet the real estate lobby, shortsighted and utterly selfish, continues to cry \"socialism\" in a last effort to smother the real facts and real issues","explanation":"Both frame private business interests as using misleading pressure tactics to displace factual or merits-based government decision-making."}]}
